text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this crucial Premier League fixture as Everton face Wolves at Goodison Park!
It sounds ludicrous to be describing matches as 'must-win' in August, but Everton and Wolves will be under no illusions as to the importance of this game.
Both sides have started the campaign with back-to-back defeats, with Sean Dyche's Toffees being thrashed 4-0 at Aston Villa last time out.
Everton have endured a difficult transfer window and have plenty of injuries to contend with here – three points would really lift the glum mood at Goodison.
It's been a similar story for Wolves, who are still awaiting their first points under Gary O'Neil.
Despite a lack of transfer activity, they produced a positive display at Manchester United on matchday one, only to be undone by poor finishing and the controversial denial of a late penalty.

The mood at Molineux took a turn for the worse last week as Wolves were outclassed in a 4-1 defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion, and they will know the importance of this tussle with a potential relegation rival.
Dyche makes three changes to the team that started at Villa Park, with two of them being enforced as Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Alex Iwobi join Dwight McNeil in the treatment room.
Danjuma makes his first start for the club in attack, while 20-year-old Dobbin is also brought in and Branthwaite replaces Keane in defence.
New arrival Chermiti is among the substitutes.
O'Neil makes two changes to his lineup for this game.
Wolves' week has been dominated by suggestions Matheus Nunes may join Manchester City in a £60million deal, and he is suspended here after picking up two yellow cards against Brighton.
Hwang replaces him out wide, while Bueno comes in for Ait-Nouri at left-back and Jonny – who looked set to be sold earlier in the window – is named on the bench.
Wolves have won their last two away league games against Everton, as many as they had in their previous 16 such visits to Goodison Park (D5 L9).
Could they win three successive matches on this ground for the very first time? The teams are out, and we're about to find out!
We're under way for this huge clash on Merseyside! Cunha gets the ball rolling for Wolves, who are kitted out in their red change strip.
Everton are looking to press high and put Wolves under pressure in the early exchanges.
Keeping the Goodison Park crowd on side will be key for the Toffees here.
Silva wins a free-kick on the left flank for Wolves, which is lifted to the back post by Bueno.
Lemina gets his head to it, but it drops comfortably into the arms of Pickford.
Cunha races into the area as Wolves break, but he is forced wide and Tarkowski eventually steps across to make a strong challenge.
The play is then stopped for Silva to receive treatment after he was caught by Patterson, but the Wolves striker is soon back to his feet.
Danjuma finds space for a shot from 25 yards out... but he lifts his effort well over Sa's crossbar.
It's been a very competitive start here, with both teams looking to be physical in the middle of the park.
Everton have lost both of their Premier League games so far this season without scoring a single goal.
The Toffees last lost their opening three games of a league campaign in 1990-91, and they have never done so without scoring.
Wolves are furious as Hwang appears to be tripped deep inside his own territory and the referee plays on.
Gueye sees a shot blocked before Patterson looks for Onana with a deep cross... but it runs away for a goal-kick.
Following defeats against Manchester United and Brighton, Wolves could lose their opening three games in a Premier League season for a second time in the last three campaigns.
They also did so in 2021-22, though they went on to finish 10th under Bruno Lage that season.
Wolves create a three-on-three on the break, but Silva's slack pass is too short for Neto and Branthwaite gets across to cut it out.
The visitors regain possession, however, penning Everton back.
The game opens up as Bueno is dispossessed and Everton counter, with Dawson heading Danjuma's initial cross away.
The hosts keep the pressure on, but Dobbin slices a left-wing delivery behind under no pressure.
POST! But wait... the flag is up! Danjuma breaks through on goal from Onana's pass.
He looks for the bottom-left corner, but Sa gets a slight touch to divert the ball onto the inside of the post before the flag is belatedly raised.
Danjuma and Sa didn't know that would be the case, however!
This has been a positive start for Everton.
Wolves are struggling to play their way through the Toffees' press, though neither team has shown much quality in the final third.
Alex Iwobi had appeared in 52 consecutive Premier League games for Everton before being ruled out of this one through injury.
Dobbin is looking to fill his boots out wide today, and the Toffees need a big performance from the youngster.
Dobbin faces up Semedo inside the area and looks to beat the full-back on the outside.
Semedo gets a touch to the ball and prods it behind for an Everton corner.
That's a waste from Everton.
Young's corner is floated straight into the hands of Sa, who was unchallenged.
We've only seen one shot on target – from Everton – so far.
This game always looked likely to be tense and cagey, given the tricky predicaments both teams find themselves in.
Neto looks to trick his way past Onana on the edge of the box, but the Everton man wins the ball and gets his team moving.
A long ball is launched forwards for Danjuma, but Dawson shepherds it back to Sa.
Cunha and Gomes combine to release Neto on the break.
He gets into the area and lifts a right-footed cross into the six-yard box, but Patterson gets back to head it clear.
Hwang is left in a heap off the pitch following a firm challenge from Patterson near the corner flag.
The referee ignores Wolves' appeals for a foul and awards an Everton goal-kick, but that looks to be a sore one for the South Korea international.
He's back to his feet after receiving some treatment.
HUGE CHANCE FOR EVERTON! How is it not 1-0? The hosts win a corner on the left, which is cleared out to Garner.

His powerful strike hits Dobbin and forces Sa into a reflex save, before Tarkowski lashes the rebound into the side netting with the goal gaping! There was a suspicion of offside, but he still should have buried that!

events.action: lashes the rebound into the side net

text: Gomes goes into the book for delaying the restart after Semedo fouls Danjuma on the Everton left.
Young's free-kick delivery is decent, but Branthwaite's glancing header is always heading off target.
Dyche will be pleased with this spell of pressure from Everton, however.
We're past the half-hour mark at Goodison, where Wolves are struggling with Everton's physicality.
The Toffees will feel they should be ahead after a glaring miss from Tarkowski.
Neto exchanges passes with Semedo to break in behind Young, but the winger's touch towards the area is far too heavy and Branthwaite can slide in to clear.
Wolves' attack has not clicked so far.
Bueno gets forward on the underlap before crossing for Neto, who tees up Gomes for a blocked shot.
It rebounds back to Neto, who shifts the ball onto his right foot before lifting a wild effort over the bar.
At last, some attacking threat from the visitors.
BIG CHANCE! Dawson is caught beneath Patterson's right-wing cross, allowing Danjuma to meet the ball unmarked with a half-volley from near the penalty spot.
He looks destined to score, but he rolls his effort wide of the bottom-right corner!
Cunha and Silva have managed just 12 and 10 touches respectively so far.
Wolves' only real attacking outlet has been Neto, who looks to fancy his chances against Everton left-back young.
Semedo, who was not booked for his earlier foul on Danjuma, is cautioned for a lunge on Dobbin.
On second viewing, the right-back seemed to get the ball, and he feels hard done by.
Tarkowski meets Young's free-kick from the left, but his tame header comes off Silva and rolls straight to Sa.
Lemina holds off three blue shirts in midfield to get Wolves moving, but Hwang's cross is slightly too high for Cunha, who heads well wide.
The Brazilian is in some discomfort after landing awkwardly – this is a huge concern for Wolves.
Cunha is still receiving treatment on the turf.
Tarkowski inadvertently stepped on Cunha's leg as the pair landed after battling for a cross into the area.
Cunha is helped to his feet and looks okay to continue after receiving treatment.
Wolves have lost several attacking players in this transfer window, so they can't afford to lose anyone to injury.
Two additional minutes will be played here.
Onana heads a long kick from Pickford down on the edge of the area.
Doucoure attempts to reach it, but Dawson and Kilman combine to hack it clear.
HALF-TIME: EVERTON 0-0 WOLVES.
Craig Pawson's half-time whistle sounds, and it's still goalless between Everton and Wolves at Goodison Park.
As many expected, it's been a tight, cagey affair lacking quality in the final third, but Dyche's hosts have created the better chances.
Both Tarkowski and Danjuma have squandered good opportunities, while Wolves have lacked inspiration with Neto their only consistent threat.
There's surely more to come from both teams after the break!
Wolves and Everton scored just 31 and 34 Premier League goals last season respectively – fewer than Erling Haaland managed for Manchester City! You can certainly see why.
Everton have only hit the target with two of their eight shots, while Wolves are yet to work Pickford from six attempts.
One goal might be enough to win this one.
O'Neil has made a change at the break.
Hwang has failed to emerge after going down under Patterson's challenge shortly before half-time.
Ait-Nouri will take his place in a more advanced position than usual on the left.
Doucoure gets the ball rolling for the second half.
Will we get a winner in this early-season basement battle?
Hwang has scored each of Wolves' last two Premier League goals (against Everton in May and Brighton last week).
How will the visitors cope after being forced to withdraw the South Korean?
Semedo fouls Dobbin on the Everton left.
The Wolves right-back needs to be careful after being booked shortly before the break.
A promising break looks to be on for Wolves as Cunha finds Bueno advancing down the left, but he checks back and concedes possession with a slack pass.
They need to be sharper in those situations.
Now Cunha finds Bueno running in behind with a cheeky ball around the corner, but the left-back is chased back by Patterson and only cross behind while on the stretch.
Doucoure cuts inside from the left, but instead of going for the shot, he attempts to find Garner.
His cross is narrowly behind the former Manchester United midfielder, who is unable to turn it goalwards.
Both teams need to make better decisions in attack.
Lemina is booked for delaying the restart after a foul from Silva.
Everton have a free-kick slightly to the left of centre, 35 yards from goal.
Everton almost catch Wolves out! Young's clever free-kick over the wall finds Danjuma, who prods goalwards.
His shot almost squirms under Sa, but the Wolves goalkeeper gets it behind for a corner.

SA KEEPS IT 0-0! Sa gets out to punch the corner as far as Garner before making a fine double save! He blocks Garner's volley, before getting behind Branthwaite's rebound and holding the ball at the second attempt.
Everton are upping the ante!
Branthwaite sees yellow for a cynical pull to stop a Wolves counter-attack.
There's a moment of concern for Everton as Onana stays down after winning possession from Neto, having appeared to get his studs caught in the turf.
He receives treatment before re-entering the action, however, and he looks okay to play on.
Patterson (41) and Semedo (54) – the two teams' respective right-backs – managed more touches than any of their team-mates in the opening 45 minutes.
That tells you something about the lack of creativity on display.
Goaaaal....
But wait, the flag is up! What a let-off for Everton! Bueno's cross is delicately prodded home by Silva, darting across Branthwaite towards the front post.
However, the linesman signals for offside, and replays show the Wolves man went slightly too early.
Silva went a fraction too early as he looked to reach Bueno's cross, but the finish was expertly applied.
That should offer some encouragement to Wolves, who are finally looking to up the intensity of their play.
WHAT A CHANCE FOR WOLVES! Pickford and Tarkowski both leave a loose ball for one another, allowing Silva to remain onside as he darts through on goal.
The Wolves striker has to score, but he side-foots just wide of the far post.
Another left-off for the hosts.
This game is being played at a much quicker pace now, with Wolves starting to show more attacking intent.
Ait-Nouri steps inside Garner and is tripped, winning a free-kick on the Wolves left.
Garner is booked after conceding that free-kick, which will be taken by Neto.
WHAT A SAVE! Neto's wicked delivery hits an Everton defender and bounces goalwards, only for Pickford to make a stunning reflex save, diving down to his right to keep the match goalless.
Now Everton go close! Doucoure puts Danjuma through, but Dawson does well to slow his advance and force him wide, from where he is unable to beat Sa.
We've got a game on our hands now!
Everton introduce former Sporting CP attacker Chermiti for his debut, with Dobbin being withdrawn.
SA MAKES A BREATHTAKING SAVE! Oh my word, how has he kept that out?! Patterson's cross bounces for Doucoure at the far post, and he goes for goal with a diving header.
Sa is completely wrongfooted, but he somehow twists his body to tip the ball up and over the bar.
That is an incredible piece of goalkeeping.
Somehow, it's still 0-0.
Doucoure does well to press high and win possession, before being chopped down by Dawson.
The Wolves defender goes into the book, but the resulting free-kick is delivered straight to Sa.
That's fabulous defending from Branthwaite, who sticks with Neto to emerge with possession as Wolves were looking to break.
The Everton youngster has done well after replacing Keane.
Everton win a corner on the left, but Sa comes through the crowd to claim it before sending Neto racing away with a great kick.
Lacking support, the winger cuts inside Danjuma and is fouled, giving Wolves a chance to deliver a free-kick into the box.
Lemina mis-controls from Neto's delivery and Doucoure breaks for Everton.
He looks to deliver an early cross for Danjuma, but Sa does well to smother the loose ball.
Wolves introduce Sarabia for Silva.
The youngster should have put Wolves ahead when released one-on-one earlier.
Cunha will likely operate further forward now.
This game has a basketball feel to it now.
A goal in the final 15 minutes or so would be huge for either team.
Chermiti forces Bueno to clear out of play inside the Wolves half.
He has gone up front since being introduced by Dyche, with Danjuma moving to his more natural left-wing role.
GOAAAAAL! But the flag goes up again, this time to deny Everton! Garner and Chermiti link up before the former finds Doucoure, who steps inside to curl a shot under Sa and in.
The flag goes up with Doucoure appearing to be slightly ahead of Dawson when the pass was played.
The VAR will take a look!
NO GOAL! The review is over.
Doucoure's right foot was slightly ahead of Dawson as he stepped onto that pass.
That's a goal ruled out at either end now!
Though it's still goalless, Everton have gotten themselves back on top in recent minutes.
O'Neil looks set to introduce another central defender in Toti.
Wolves are still yet to record a shot on target in this game, sending all eight of their attempts wayward.
The visitors are looking a little short of ideas.
Sa catches a deep cross from Patterson and immediately looks to send Cunha running in behind, but his kick runs all the way through to Pickford.
Wolves are making a double change.
Toti replaces Bueno at left-back.
Cunha is also, perhaps surprisingly, withdrawn.
Towering striker Kalajdzic takes his place up front.
Wolves appeal for handball as Chermiti chests down a driven pass before winning a corner off Dawson.
Young's set-piece is poor, however, and Branthwaite can only hook it well wide.

GOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAAL!!!! KALAJDZIC PUTS WOLVES AHEAD! The towering striker has his first Premier League goal just minutes after coming off the bench! Neto swings a deep cross in from the right, which the six-foot-seven striker glances beyond Pickford.
What a huge goal that could be for O'Neil's men.
1-0 Wolves!
Neto had few options when he picked up possession on the right, but he stepped inside to find the head of Kalajdzic with a terrific cross!
A late Ait-Nouri goal handed Wolves their first victory under Julen Lopetegui on this ground on Boxing Day last year.
Is O'Neil about to replicate his predecessor by getting off the mark at Goodison? Everton have two minutes plus stoppage time to hit back.
Dawson cleverly wins a foul off Chermiti near his own corner flag, and the Everton striker goes into the book.
We're into FIVE additional minutes at Goodison.
Can Wolves hold on? Everton are preparing further changes.
Young forward Cannon replaces Danjuma.
Keane is also on, presumably to be used as an auxiliary striker.
Gueye makes way.
Everton are penning Wolves back and flinging crosses into the area now.
Keane feels his shirt was being pulled as he sees a shot blocked on the turn, before Sa claims Young's delivery.
Wolves have a chance to kill the contest as Sarabia capitalises on Tarkowski's slip and heads for goal, but he is crowded out on the edge of the box.
Wolves then win a throw on the left, which will allow them to eat up some valuable seconds.
Sarabia links up with Kalajdzic before being fouled on the edge of Everton's area.
Surely Wolves have done enough to pick up their first win of the season?
Sarabia goes for goal from the free-kick, and Pickford springs to his right to push it away.
Everton hoist the ball forward, looking to construct one last attack...
FULL-TIME: EVERTON 0-1 WOLVES.

The full-time whistle sounds at Goodison Park, and Wolves are off the mark for the 2023-24 season with a vital 1-0 win over Everton! Substitute Kalajdzic was the hero, glancing Neto's cross home for his first goal in English football just over two minutes after entering the fray.
What a moment for the Austrian, who suffered a serious injury on his Wolves debut last season and missed the rest of his first campaign with the club.
Everton are left to rue several missed chances yet again, with Doucoure somehow being denied by a spectacular save from Sa when the game was goalless.
It's a familiar story for Everton, who managed 15 shots to Wolves' 11, and seven attempts on target to the visitors' two, without finding the net.
They desperately need to find a source of goals, having lost their first three games of a league season without scoring for the very first time.
The Toffees' next league game is another big one at Sheffield United next Saturday.
Wolves go to Crystal Palace one day later.
We hope you have enjoyed our live coverage of a dramatic Premier League win for Wolves.
It's goodbye from us, and we'll catch you next time.
